text: I am continuing to read journals and other reference materials to increase and improve my knowledge in the areas of pharmacology and biochemistry so that I not only have a better perspective of the project areas in the Biochemical Division, but can provide meaningful input to these project areas also.
At present this need is far exceeded by the actual project work in both the cell culture and analytical method areas.
I attended an in-house short course on basic gas chromatography taught by Dr. Harold McNair.
I found this course to be helpful in general, but not directed toward the specific areas of interest to me.
Several techniques described by Dr. Hank Purvine during his seminar on poisons are applicable to our future investigations and I appreciate the opportunity to attend this type presentation.
The development of a routine GC analysis for plasma nicotine and cotinine is proceeding on schedule.
Dr. Alice Lynn has committed to having purified sets of nicotine, cotinine, and analogs for internal standards to me by mid-July.
Recovery studies will begin and a comparison of at least two and possibly three extraction procedures will begin.
Completion of the extraction work will be followed by several serum/plasma analyses using standard addition techniques.
Presently an evaluation of packed column versus fused silica capillary column chromatography has been completed.
